examInfo.title: CTFL - V4.0 - EN - SAMPLE EXAM - MODEL A

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes a primary objective of testing?

options.label: a
options.text: To prove that the software is free of all defects

options.label: b
options.text: To demonstrate that the software works correctly in all situations

options.label: c
options.text: To reduce the risk of inadequate software quality

options.label: d
options.text: To ensure the software is delivered on time and within budget

a.explanation: Testing cannot prove the absence of all defects; it can only detect the presence of defects.

b.explanation: Demonstrating that software works in all situations implies exhaustive testing, which is impossible.

c.explanation: A primary objective of testing is to reduce the risk of inadequate software quality, thereby providing confidence in the quality of the software.

d.explanation: Delivery timelines and budgets are project management concerns, not primary testing objectives.

questions.questionText: Which testing principle states that testing can show the presence of defects but cannot prove their absence?

options.label: a
options.text: Exhaustive testing is impossible

options.label: b
options.text: Testing shows the presence of defects, not their absence

options.label: c
options.text: Defect clustering

options.label: d
options.text: Pesticide paradox

a.explanation: Exhaustive testing being impossible is the second principle, not the one about showing presence vs absence.

b.explanation: The first principle of testing states that testing can show the presence of defects but it cannot prove that there are no defects.

c.explanation: Defect clustering refers to the observation that most defects are found in a small number of modules.

d.explanation: The pesticide paradox states that if the same tests are repeated, they will eventually no longer find new defects.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of the 'pesticide paradox' testing principle?

options.label: a
options.text: A critical module has been found to contain most of the defects in a system

options.label: b
options.text: The test team discovers that running the same regression tests over time finds fewer new defects

options.label: c
options.text: The test team cannot test every possible combination of inputs

options.label: d
options.text: Testing early in development is more cost-effective than testing later

a.explanation: This describes defect clustering, where defects tend to concentrate in specific modules.

b.explanation: The pesticide paradox states that if the same tests are continually repeated, they will stop finding new defects. Tests need to be reviewed and updated.

c.explanation: This describes the principle that exhaustive testing is impossible.

d.explanation: This describes the principle that early testing saves time and money.

questions.questionText: Which of the following activities is part of the test implementation activity?

options.label: a
options.text: Identifying test conditions

options.label: b
options.text: Creating test suites from test cases

options.label: c
options.text: Analyzing the test basis

options.label: d
options.text: Evaluating exit criteria

a.explanation: Identifying test conditions is part of test analysis.

b.explanation: Test implementation includes organizing test cases into test suites, preparing test data, and creating test scripts.

c.explanation: Analyzing the test basis is part of test analysis, not test implementation.

d.explanation: Evaluating exit criteria is part of test monitoring and control, or test completion.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of testware?

options.label: a
options.text: Source code of the system under test

options.label: b
options.text: Test progress reports

options.label: c
options.text: Business requirements from the customer

options.label: d
options.text: Sprint planning notes

a.explanation: Source code is the work product being tested, not testware.

b.explanation: Testware includes any work product created during the test process, such as test plans, test cases, test data, test scripts, and test reports.

c.explanation: Business requirements are input documents for testing, not testware produced by the test process.

d.explanation: Sprint planning notes are project management artifacts, not testware.

questions.questionText: What is the PRIMARY difference between errors, defects, and failures in software testing?

options.label: a
options.text: Errors are found in production; defects are found in testing; failures are found in requirements

options.label: b
options.text: An error is a human mistake that may cause a defect; a defect may lead to a failure when executed

options.label: c
options.text: Errors and defects are synonymous; failures are defects that have been verified

options.label: d
options.text: A defect is always more severe than a failure

a.explanation: This incorrectly associates each term with a specific phase; errors can happen at any stage.

b.explanation: An error (mistake) made by a human produces a defect in the code. When the defective code is executed, a failure may occur. This is the correct causal chain.

c.explanation: Errors and defects are not synonymous; they represent different concepts in the fault chain.

d.explanation: Severity is not used to distinguish between defects and failures in this way.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the 'absence-of-errors fallacy' testing principle?

options.label: a
options.text: Finding and fixing many defects does not help if the system is unusable or does not meet user needs

options.label: b
options.text: A system with no reported defects is guaranteed to meet user requirements

options.label: c
options.text: Testing can prove that a system has no defects

options.label: d
options.text: Users never find defects that testers missed

a.explanation: The absence-of-errors fallacy states that finding and fixing defects is of no use if the system built does not fulfill users' needs and expectations.

b.explanation: A system with no reported defects may still fail to meet user needs, which is exactly what this principle warns against.

c.explanation: Testing cannot prove the absence of defects; that is the first testing principle.

d.explanation: Users do find defects in production that testers missed; this is not related to this principle.

questions.questionText: Which role is PRIMARILY responsible for planning and coordinating the overall testing effort?

options.label: a
options.text: Tester

options.label: b
options.text: Developer

options.label: c
options.text: Test manager

options.label: d
options.text: Business analyst

a.explanation: Testers are responsible for creating and executing test cases, not for planning the overall testing effort.

b.explanation: Developers write code and may perform unit testing, but they are not primarily responsible for coordinating the testing effort.

c.explanation: The test manager (or test lead) is primarily responsible for planning, organizing, and leading the test activities and providing the overall direction of testing.

d.explanation: Business analysts focus on requirements, not on coordinating testing activities.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a benefit of early testing (shift-left)?

options.label: a
options.text: Defects are more expensive to fix early in development

options.label: b
options.text: Requirements defects can be detected before code is written

options.label: c
options.text: Testing can be skipped in later phases when early testing is thorough

options.label: d
options.text: Test documentation is not needed when testing early

a.explanation: The opposite is true: defects are cheaper to fix when found early.

b.explanation: Early testing allows detection of defects in requirements, design, and other artifacts before code is written, saving significant rework costs.

c.explanation: Early testing does not eliminate the need for later testing phases; each level serves a different purpose.

d.explanation: Test documentation is always important regardless of when testing begins.

questions.questionText: Which SDLC model emphasizes testing at each development phase, with corresponding test levels mirroring development activities?

options.label: a
options.text: Waterfall model

options.label: b
options.text: V-model

options.label: c
options.text: Spiral model

options.label: d
options.text: Kanban model

a.explanation: The waterfall model is sequential and typically defers testing to after development is complete.

b.explanation: The V-model (Verification and Validation model) explicitly pairs each development phase with a corresponding test level, emphasizing early test planning.

c.explanation: The spiral model focuses on risk management through iterative development cycles.

d.explanation: Kanban is an agile framework focused on flow and limiting work in progress, not on pairing test levels with development phases.

questions.questionText: Which test level focuses on testing the interfaces and interactions between integrated components?

options.label: a
options.text: Component testing

options.label: b
options.text: Component integration testing

options.label: c
options.text: System testing

options.label: d
options.text: Acceptance testing

a.explanation: Component testing (unit testing) focuses on individual components in isolation.

b.explanation: Component integration testing focuses on testing the interfaces and interactions between components that have been integrated together.

c.explanation: System testing focuses on the behavior and capabilities of a whole system.

d.explanation: Acceptance testing focuses on validating whether the system meets user needs and business requirements.

questions.questionText: What is the PRIMARY purpose of regression testing?

options.label: a
options.text: To confirm that a specific defect has been fixed

options.label: b
options.text: To verify that changes have not introduced new defects in unchanged areas

options.label: c
options.text: To test the system for the first time in a new environment

options.label: d
options.text: To evaluate non-functional characteristics of the system

a.explanation: Confirming a specific defect has been fixed is the purpose of confirmation testing (re-testing), not regression testing.

b.explanation: Regression testing verifies that changes to the software (bug fixes, enhancements) have not caused previously working features to fail.

c.explanation: Testing in a new environment is part of system integration testing or operational acceptance testing.

d.explanation: Evaluating non-functional characteristics is the purpose of non-functional testing.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a trigger for maintenance testing?

options.label: a
options.text: The software has been freshly developed and is being tested for the first time

options.label: b
options.text: Migration of the application to a new operating system platform

options.label: c
options.text: Requirements are being analyzed for a new product

options.label: d
options.text: Developers are fixing compilation errors found during code review

a.explanation: Testing a freshly developed software is initial development testing, not maintenance testing.

b.explanation: Maintenance testing is triggered by modifications, migrations, or retirement of software. Migration to a new platform is a classic maintenance testing trigger.

c.explanation: Analyzing requirements for a new product is part of the development lifecycle, not maintenance.

d.explanation: Fixing compilation errors is part of development, not a trigger for maintenance testing.

questions.questionText: What does shift-left testing mean in the context of an SDLC?

options.label: a
options.text: Moving testing responsibilities from developers to dedicated testers

options.label: b
options.text: Starting testing activities earlier in the development lifecycle

options.label: c
options.text: Moving tests from the left column to the right column in a test matrix

options.label: d
options.text: Removing test activities from the end of the project

a.explanation: Shift-left is about when testing occurs in the timeline, not about who performs it.

b.explanation: Shift-left means starting test activities earlier in the SDLC — ideally during requirements and design phases — to detect defects sooner when they are cheaper to fix.

c.explanation: This is not a recognized meaning of shift-left in software testing.

d.explanation: Shift-left adds test activities earlier, it does not remove activities from the end.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST distinguishes static testing from dynamic testing?

options.label: a
options.text: Static testing executes the software; dynamic testing does not

options.label: b
options.text: Static testing does not execute the software; dynamic testing does

options.label: c
options.text: Static testing is performed only by developers; dynamic testing is performed only by testers

options.label: d
options.text: Static testing finds failures; dynamic testing finds defects

a.explanation: This is the reverse: it is dynamic testing that executes the software.

b.explanation: Static testing examines work products (code, requirements, designs) without executing them. Dynamic testing executes the software and observes behavior.

c.explanation: Both static and dynamic testing can be performed by various roles; neither is exclusively assigned to developers or testers.

d.explanation: Static testing finds defects; dynamic testing finds failures. It is the other way around from what is stated.

questions.questionText: Which review type is the MOST formal and follows a defined process with trained roles and entry/exit criteria?

options.label: a
options.text: Informal review

options.label: b
options.text: Walkthrough

options.label: c
options.text: Technical review

options.label: d
options.text: Inspection

a.explanation: Informal reviews are the least formal, with no documented process or checklist required.

b.explanation: Walkthroughs are led by the author and are moderately formal but do not require trained roles.

c.explanation: Technical reviews are peer-led and more formal than walkthroughs, but less rigorous than inspections.

d.explanation: Inspection is the most formal review type, with defined entry/exit criteria, trained roles (moderator, scribe, etc.), and a formal process for defect detection and follow-up.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a benefit of static testing compared to dynamic testing?

options.label: a
options.text: Static testing can detect failures that only appear at runtime

options.label: b
options.text: Static testing can detect defects in non-executable artifacts like requirements and design documents

options.label: c
options.text: Static testing requires a running version of the software

options.label: d
options.text: Static testing is always more effective than dynamic testing

a.explanation: Runtime failures can only be detected by dynamic testing, not static testing.

b.explanation: A key benefit of static testing is the ability to find defects in non-executable artifacts such as requirements, designs, user stories, and plans before any code is written.

c.explanation: Static testing does NOT require a running version of the software; this is what distinguishes it from dynamic testing.

d.explanation: Static and dynamic testing are complementary; neither is always more effective than the other.

questions.questionText: During which review activity are defects discussed with the author and decisions made about their disposition?

options.label: a
options.text: Planning

options.label: b
options.text: Individual review

options.label: c
options.text: Communication and analysis

options.label: d
options.text: Fixing and reporting

a.explanation: Planning involves determining scope, objectives, and logistics of the review, not discussing defects.

b.explanation: Individual review is where reviewers examine the work product on their own and note issues, before the group meeting.

c.explanation: During communication and analysis (the review meeting), anomalies found are discussed with the author, and the review team decides their status and ownership.

d.explanation: Fixing and reporting is when the author fixes the defects and the moderator tracks the status of fixes.

questions.questionText: A tester is designing test cases for a function that accepts a numeric input in the range 1-100. Using equivalence partitioning, which of the following test inputs represents a valid partition?

a.explanation: 0 is below the valid range (1-100), so it belongs to an invalid partition.

b.explanation: 50 is within the valid range (1-100), making it a representative value from the valid equivalence partition.

c.explanation: 101 is above the valid range, so it belongs to an invalid partition.

d.explanation: -5 is a negative value below the valid range, belonging to an invalid partition.

questions.questionText: A field accepts values from 10 to 20 inclusive. Using 2-value boundary value analysis, which set of values should be tested?

a.explanation: 2-value BVA tests the boundary values and their immediate neighbors just outside. For range 10-20: the boundaries are 10 and 20, and the values just outside are 9 and 21.

b.explanation: This includes the midpoint (15) but misses the out-of-boundary values (9 and 21) required by 2-value BVA.

c.explanation: This tests values one step inside the boundary (11, 19) instead of the actual boundary values (10, 20).

d.explanation: This only tests the boundary values themselves but misses the out-of-boundary values (9 and 21) required by 2-value BVA.

questions.questionText: A decision table has 3 conditions, each with 2 possible values (True/False). How many rules (columns) does a full decision table have?

a.explanation: 3 rules would only cover the number of conditions, not all combinations.

b.explanation: 6 would result from multiplying 3 x 2, but the correct formula is 2^3.

c.explanation: With 3 conditions each having 2 values, the full decision table has 2^3 = 8 rules, covering all possible combinations.

d.explanation: 9 would result from 3^2, which is not the correct formula for binary conditions.

questions.questionText: In state transition testing, what does a transition represent?

options.label: a
options.text: A condition that the system must satisfy before entering a state

options.label: b
options.text: A move from one state to another triggered by an event and possibly a guard condition

options.label: c
options.text: An output action that always occurs when the system is in a given state

options.label: d
options.text: A static snapshot of the system at a particular point in time

a.explanation: This describes a guard condition or entry condition, not a transition.

b.explanation: A transition in a state diagram represents the movement from one state to another, triggered by an event, and optionally constrained by a guard condition, with an optional associated action.

c.explanation: This describes an activity (action) within a state, not a transition.

d.explanation: A state represents the system's condition at a point in time; a transition is the movement between states.

questions.questionText: Which white-box technique measures whether every executable statement in the code has been executed at least once?

options.label: a
options.text: Branch coverage

options.label: b
options.text: Statement coverage

options.label: c
options.text: Path coverage

options.label: d
options.text: Condition coverage

a.explanation: Branch coverage measures whether every branch (true/false outcome of every decision) has been executed.

b.explanation: Statement coverage measures the percentage of executable statements that have been executed by the test suite.

c.explanation: Path coverage measures whether every possible path through the code has been executed, which is generally impractical.

d.explanation: Condition coverage measures whether each individual condition in a decision has been evaluated to both true and false.

questions.questionText: Which experience-based test technique involves the tester actively exploring the application and simultaneously designing, executing, and logging tests?

options.label: a
options.text: Error guessing

options.label: b
options.text: Checklist-based testing

options.label: c
options.text: Exploratory testing

options.label: d
options.text: Boundary value analysis

a.explanation: Error guessing uses the tester's knowledge and experience to anticipate likely defects, but test cases are designed before execution.

b.explanation: Checklist-based testing uses a predefined list of items to check and is less dynamic than exploratory testing.

c.explanation: Exploratory testing is a simultaneous activity of test design and execution, where the tester learns about the system while exploring it and adapts their approach dynamically.

d.explanation: Boundary value analysis is a black-box technique, not an experience-based technique.

questions.questionText: In BDD (Behavior Driven Development), which format is used to express acceptance criteria?

options.label: a
options.text: If-Then-Else

options.label: b
options.text: Given-When-Then

options.label: c
options.text: Arrange-Act-Assert

options.label: d
options.text: Setup-Execute-Verify

a.explanation: If-Then-Else is a programming construct, not the BDD format.

b.explanation: BDD uses the Given-When-Then format to express scenarios: Given (context/precondition), When (action/event), Then (expected outcome).

c.explanation: Arrange-Act-Assert is a pattern used in unit testing, not specifically in BDD.

d.explanation: Setup-Execute-Verify is not the standard BDD format.

questions.questionText: Which test technique would be MOST appropriate when testing a field that only accepts the values 'Red', 'Green', and 'Blue'?

options.label: a
options.text: Boundary value analysis

options.label: b
options.text: State transition testing

options.label: c
options.text: Equivalence partitioning

options.label: d
options.text: Decision table testing

a.explanation: Boundary value analysis is for ordered partitions with numeric boundaries, not discrete enumerated values.

b.explanation: State transition testing is for systems that move between states based on events, not for simple field validation.

c.explanation: Equivalence partitioning divides inputs into partitions. Here there is one valid partition (Red, Green, Blue) and an invalid partition (any other value).

d.explanation: Decision table testing is best suited for combinations of conditions that produce different actions, not for a single field with discrete values.

questions.questionText: What is the PRIMARY purpose of a test plan?

options.label: a
options.text: To record defects found during test execution

options.label: b
options.text: To document the means and schedule for achieving test objectives

options.label: c
options.text: To list all test cases and their expected results

options.label: d
options.text: To report the final test results to stakeholders

a.explanation: Defects are recorded in defect reports, not in the test plan.

b.explanation: A test plan documents the means, resources, and schedule for achieving test objectives. It describes the scope, approach, resources, and schedule of intended test activities.

c.explanation: Test cases are documented in test specifications, not in the test plan.

d.explanation: Final test results are reported in the test completion report, not the test plan.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes product risk in software testing?

options.label: a
options.text: The risk that the project will be delivered late or over budget

options.label: b
options.text: The risk that a work product may fail to satisfy its stakeholders' legitimate needs

options.label: c
options.text: The risk associated with insufficient testing resources

options.label: d
options.text: The risk of conflicts between team members during the project

a.explanation: Late delivery and budget overruns are project risks, not product risks.

b.explanation: Product risk is the risk that a work product (such as the software under test) may fail to satisfy legitimate stakeholder needs, including functional and non-functional aspects.

c.explanation: Insufficient testing resources are project risks, not product risks.

d.explanation: Team conflicts are project risks related to people management, not product risks.

questions.questionText: A team uses story points and velocity data from previous sprints to estimate test effort. Which estimation approach is this?

options.label: a
options.text: Expert-based estimation

options.label: b
options.text: Metric-based estimation

options.label: c
options.text: Planning poker

options.label: d
options.text: Three-point estimation

a.explanation: Expert-based estimation relies on the judgment and experience of experts, not on historical data.

b.explanation: Metric-based estimation uses data collected from previous projects or previous iterations of the same project (such as velocity and story points) to calculate estimates.

c.explanation: Planning poker is a technique for expert-based estimation through consensus, not metric-based.

d.explanation: Three-point estimation uses optimistic, pessimistic, and most likely estimates, typically from experts.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a test metric used to monitor test progress?

options.label: a
options.text: Number of requirements in scope

options.label: b
options.text: Percentage of test cases executed

options.label: c
options.text: Number of developers on the team

options.label: d
options.text: Total lines of code in the application

a.explanation: Number of requirements is a scope metric, not a test progress metric.

b.explanation: Percentage of test cases executed is a standard test progress metric that helps monitor how far along the test execution is.

c.explanation: Team size is a project resource metric, not a test progress metric.

d.explanation: Lines of code is a code metric, not a test progress metric.

questions.questionText: Which document is produced at the END of a test level or the entire testing effort and summarizes test results and recommendations?

options.label: a
options.text: Test plan

options.label: b
options.text: Test progress report

options.label: c
options.text: Test completion report

options.label: d
options.text: Defect report

a.explanation: The test plan is created at the start of testing and documents the approach and schedule.

b.explanation: Test progress reports are produced periodically during test execution to communicate current status.

c.explanation: The test completion report is produced at the end of a test level or the entire project, summarizing what was tested, results achieved, defects found, and lessons learned.

d.explanation: Defect reports document individual defects found during testing, not overall test results.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about configuration management in testing is CORRECT?

options.label: a
options.text: Configuration management is only needed for code, not for test documentation

options.label: b
options.text: Configuration management ensures that testware is traceable, version-controlled, and reproducible

options.label: c
options.text: Configuration management eliminates the need for defect tracking

options.label: d
options.text: Configuration management replaces the test plan

a.explanation: Configuration management applies to all work products, including test plans, test cases, and test data, not just code.

b.explanation: Configuration management provides traceability, version control, and ensures that testware can be reproduced and related back to specific versions of the software.

c.explanation: Configuration management and defect tracking serve different purposes; neither replaces the other.

d.explanation: Configuration management is a support process; it does not replace planning documents.

questions.questionText: What information is typically included in a defect report?

options.label: a
options.text: The list of all passed test cases

options.label: b
options.text: A unique identifier, summary, severity, steps to reproduce, and actual vs expected results

options.label: c
options.text: The complete source code of the module where the defect was found

options.label: d
options.text: The test plan version and exit criteria

a.explanation: Passed test cases are part of test execution reports, not defect reports.

b.explanation: A typical defect report includes a unique ID, title/summary, severity, priority, steps to reproduce, actual results, expected results, environment, and status.

c.explanation: Source code is not typically included in a defect report; a reference to the relevant area is sufficient.

d.explanation: Test plan version and exit criteria belong to the test plan, not the defect report.

questions.questionText: What is the difference between defect severity and defect priority?

options.label: a
options.text: Severity and priority are the same thing with different names

options.label: b
options.text: Severity is the impact on the system; priority is the urgency to fix it

options.label: c
options.text: Severity is set by the project manager; priority is set by the tester

options.label: d
options.text: Severity refers to how many users are affected; priority refers to how complex the fix is

a.explanation: Severity and priority are distinct concepts; a high-severity defect may have low priority if it is rarely triggered.

b.explanation: Severity describes the impact/criticality of a defect on the system. Priority describes the urgency of fixing the defect from a business perspective.

c.explanation: Severity is usually assigned by the tester; priority is often set by the product owner or project manager.

d.explanation: These are not the correct definitions of severity and priority.

questions.questionText: Risk-based testing prioritizes testing based on:

options.label: a
options.text: The alphabetical order of test case names

options.label: b
options.text: The likelihood and impact of potential failures

options.label: c
options.text: The order in which requirements were written

options.label: d
options.text: The personal preference of the test manager

a.explanation: Alphabetical ordering has no relevance to risk-based testing.

b.explanation: Risk-based testing prioritizes test activities based on product risks, which are determined by the likelihood of failure occurring and the impact (consequences) if it does.

c.explanation: The order of requirements has no bearing on risk levels.

d.explanation: Testing decisions should be based on objective risk criteria, not personal preference.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a BENEFIT of test automation?

options.label: a
options.text: Automated tests always find more defects than manual tests

options.label: b
options.text: Automated tests reduce repetitive manual testing effort and allow faster regression testing

options.label: c
options.text: Automated testing completely replaces exploratory testing

options.label: d
options.text: Automated tests require no maintenance after initial creation

a.explanation: Automated tests do not always find more defects; they are most effective for regression testing where the same scenarios are repeated.

b.explanation: A key benefit of automation is reducing the effort of repetitive manual testing and enabling fast, consistent regression testing.

c.explanation: Automated testing cannot replace exploratory testing, which relies on human creativity and intuition.

d.explanation: Automated tests require ongoing maintenance as the application changes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a RISK associated with test automation?

options.label: a
options.text: Test execution becomes faster

options.label: b
options.text: Unrealistic expectations about the benefits of automation

options.label: c
options.text: Consistent test execution without human error

options.label: d
options.text: Easy access to test results for all stakeholders

a.explanation: Faster test execution is a benefit, not a risk.

b.explanation: Unrealistic expectations (such as automation solving all testing problems or eliminating the need for manual testing) is a recognized risk that can lead to project failures.

c.explanation: Consistent execution is a benefit of automation, not a risk.

d.explanation: Easy access to results is a benefit of automation, not a risk.

questions.questionText: Which type of tool is used to execute tests without manual intervention by running test scripts against the system?

options.label: a
options.text: Static analysis tool

options.label: b
options.text: Test management tool

options.label: c
options.text: Test execution tool

options.label: d
options.text: Requirements management tool

a.explanation: Static analysis tools examine code without executing it, to find potential defects.

b.explanation: Test management tools organize and track test activities, cases, and results.

c.explanation: Test execution tools (also called test automation frameworks or test runners) execute test scripts automatically against the system under test.

d.explanation: Requirements management tools manage and trace requirements, not execute tests.

questions.questionText: A test team has 100% statement coverage on a module. Which of the following is a TRUE statement about this coverage?

options.label: a
options.text: All branches have also been covered

options.label: b
options.text: All defects in the module have been detected

options.label: c
options.text: Every executable statement has been executed at least once

options.label: d
options.text: The module is ready for production deployment

a.explanation: 100% statement coverage does not imply 100% branch coverage; a branch may not be taken even if its containing statement is executed.

b.explanation: Coverage metrics do not guarantee defect detection; untested combinations may still harbor defects.

c.explanation: 100% statement coverage means every executable statement in the code has been executed at least once by the test suite.

d.explanation: Coverage alone does not determine production readiness; other quality criteria must also be met.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the role of a tester in an Agile team?

options.label: a
options.text: Testers only work in a separate QA phase after development is complete

options.label: b
options.text: Testers collaborate with developers and business stakeholders throughout the sprint

options.label: c
options.text: Testers are solely responsible for writing all acceptance criteria

options.label: d
options.text: Testers only perform manual testing; automation is handled by a separate team

a.explanation: In Agile, testing is not deferred to a separate QA phase; it is integrated throughout each sprint.

b.explanation: In Agile, testers work closely with developers and business stakeholders throughout each sprint, participating in planning, review, and retrospectives.

c.explanation: Acceptance criteria are typically written collaboratively by the team including product owner, developers, and testers.

d.explanation: In Agile teams, testers are often responsible for both manual and automated testing.
